import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.55

by A. Yu. Olshanskii

The quasivarieties of groups in each of which a non-trivial identity holds form a
semigroup under the Mal'cev product. Is this semigroup free?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.55»

universe u

/-- An equation between group words in finitely many variables. -/
structure GroupIdentity where
  arity : ℕ
  lhs : FreeGroup (Fin arity)
  rhs : FreeGroup (Fin arity)

/-- A quasi-identity is a finite conjunction of equations implying an equation,
all in the same finite set of variables. -/
structure GroupQuasiIdentity where
  arity : ℕ
  premises : List (FreeGroup (Fin arity) × FreeGroup (Fin arity))
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin arity) × FreeGroup (Fin arity)

/-- A group satisfies a quasi-identity if every assignment satisfying all its
premises also satisfies its conclusion. -/
def SatisfiesQuasiIdentity (G : GrpCat.{u}) (q : GroupQuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : Fin q.arity → G,
    (∀ e ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift f e.1 = FreeGroup.lift f e.2) →
      FreeGroup.lift f q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift f q.conclusion.2

/-- An extensional class of groups that is axiomatized by group quasi-identities. -/
structure GroupQuasivariety where
  carrier : Set GrpCat.{u}
  is_axiomatizable : ∃ axioms : Set GroupQuasiIdentity,
    carrier = {G | ∀ q ∈ axioms, SatisfiesQuasiIdentity G q}

/-- A group satisfies an identity if the two words have equal values under every
assignment of its variables. -/
def SatisfiesIdentity (G : GrpCat.{u}) (i : GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : Fin i.arity → G, FreeGroup.lift f i.lhs = FreeGroup.lift f i.rhs

/-- A quasivariety satisfies a non-trivial identity if all its groups satisfy an
identity whose two words are distinct in the corresponding free group. -/
def SatisfiesNontrivialIdentity (K : GroupQuasivariety.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∃ i : GroupIdentity, i.lhs ≠ i.rhs ∧ ∀ G ∈ K.carrier, SatisfiesIdentity G i

/-- The fixed-universe set of group quasivarieties satisfying a non-trivial identity. -/
def BoundedQuasivariety := {K : GroupQuasivariety.{u} // SatisfiesNontrivialIdentity K}

/-- A subgroup, regarded as a bundled group in the same universe. -/
def subgroupModel {G : GrpCat.{u}} (N : Subgroup G) : GrpCat.{u} :=
  GrpCat.of N

/-- The quotient by a normal subgroup, regarded as a bundled group in the same universe. -/
def quotientModel {G : GrpCat.{u}} (N : Subgroup G) (hN : N.Normal) :
    GrpCat.{u} := by
  letI := hN
  exact GrpCat.of (G ⧸ N)

/-- An operation on the relevant quasivarieties is their Mal'cev product if
membership has the usual normal-subgroup characterization. -/
def IsMalcevProduct
    (mul : BoundedQuasivariety.{u} → BoundedQuasivariety.{u} →
      BoundedQuasivariety.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ K L G, G ∈ (mul K L).1.carrier ↔
    ∃ (N : Subgroup G) (hN : N.Normal),
      subgroupModel N ∈ K.1.carrier ∧ quotientModel N hN ∈ L.1.carrier

/-- A binary operation is a free-semigroup operation if it makes its carrier
isomorphic to the free semigroup on some type of generators. -/
def IsFreeSemigroupOperation {S : Type u} (mul : S → S → S) : Prop :=
  ∃ X : Type u, Nonempty (@MulEquiv S (FreeSemigroup X) ⟨mul⟩ inferInstance)

/--
Is the semigroup of group quasivarieties satisfying a non-trivial identity,
under the Mal'cev product, free? Here $G \in K L$ means that $G$ has a normal
subgroup $N \in K$ with $G/N \in L$. Quasivarieties and groups are restricted
to a fixed universe so that they form a set. The asserted semigroup premise is
represented by considering the uniquely specified Mal'cev product operation.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.55» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ᵉ (mul : BoundedQuasivariety.{u} → BoundedQuasivariety.{u} →
      BoundedQuasivariety.{u}),
      IsMalcevProduct mul → IsFreeSemigroupOperation mul := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.55»
modeling_decisions: A group quasivariety is modeled extensionally, in a fixed universe, as a set of bundled Mathlib `GrpCat` objects equal to the models of some set of finite group quasi-identities.

A non-trivial identity is an equation between distinct elements of a finitely generated free group that is satisfied by every group in the quasivariety; this expresses containment in a proper group variety.
The Mal'cev product is specified by the exact condition that G has a normal subgroup N in the left quasivariety with G/N in the right quasivariety.

Because closure and associativity of the Mal'cev product are asserted in the source preamble rather than asked, the answer proposition universally considers operations satisfying the unique Mal'cev membership specification. A reviewer should check this treatment of the asserted existence premise.
Free means multiplicatively equivalent to `FreeSemigroup X` for some generator type X, not free as a monoid. The fixed-universe collection and generator type live at the same universe level.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.55

by A. Yu. Olshanskii

The quasivarieties considered below are classes of groups axiomatized by
quasi-identities and represented using groups in one fixed universe. A
quasivariety satisfies a non-trivial identity if it is contained in a proper
variety. The product of two classes is their Mal'cev product: a group belongs
to the product when it has a normal subgroup in the first class and the
corresponding quotient belongs to the second class.

The classes of group quasivarieties satisfying a non-trivial identity form a
semigroup under this product. Is this semigroup free?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.55»

/-- A group whose carrier lies in the fixed universe used for this problem. -/
structure GroupObject where
  carrier : Type
  group : Group carrier

instance : CoeSort GroupObject Type := ⟨GroupObject.carrier⟩

instance (G : GroupObject) : Group G := G.group

/-- Bundle a group in the fixed universe as a `GroupObject`. -/
def GroupObject.of (G : Type) [Group G] : GroupObject := ⟨G, inferInstance⟩

/-- Bundle the quotient of a group by a normal subgroup. -/
def GroupObject.quotient (G : GroupObject) (N : Subgroup G) (hN : N.Normal) : GroupObject :=
  letI : N.Normal := hN
  GroupObject.of (G ⧸ N)


/-- A term in the language of groups, with variables indexed by `α`. -/
inductive GroupTerm (α : Type*) where
  | var (x : α)
  | one
  | mul (s t : GroupTerm α)
  | inv (t : GroupTerm α)

/-- Evaluation of a term in a group under an assignment of its variables. -/
def GroupTerm.eval {α G : Type*} [Group G] (v : α → G) : GroupTerm α → G
  | .var x => v x
  | .one => 1
  | .mul s t => s.eval v * t.eval v
  | .inv t => (t.eval v)⁻¹

/-- A finitary quasi-identity in the language of groups. -/
structure GroupQuasiIdentity where
  arity : ℕ
  premises : List (GroupTerm (Fin arity) × GroupTerm (Fin arity))
  conclusion : GroupTerm (Fin arity) × GroupTerm (Fin arity)

/-- A group satisfies a quasi-identity if every assignment satisfying all its
premise equations also satisfies its conclusion equation. -/
def SatisfiesQuasiIdentity (G : GroupObject) (q : GroupQuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : Fin q.arity → G,
    (∀ e ∈ q.premises, e.1.eval v = e.2.eval v) →
      q.conclusion.1.eval v = q.conclusion.2.eval v

/-- A class of groups is a quasivariety if it is precisely the class of models
of some set of quasi-identities. -/
def IsGroupQuasivariety (K : Set GroupObject) : Prop :=
  ∃ axioms : Set GroupQuasiIdentity,
    ∀ G, G ∈ K ↔ ∀ q ∈ axioms, SatisfiesQuasiIdentity G q

/-- Group quasivarieties, represented extensionally as classes of groups in a
fixed universe. -/
def GroupQuasivariety := {K : Set GroupObject // IsGroupQuasivariety K}

/-- An identity in the language of groups. -/
structure GroupIdentity where
  arity : ℕ
  lhs : GroupTerm (Fin arity)
  rhs : GroupTerm (Fin arity)

/-- A group satisfies an identity if its two terms agree under every assignment. -/
def SatisfiesIdentity (G : GroupObject) (i : GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : Fin i.arity → G, i.lhs.eval v = i.rhs.eval v

/-- An identity is non-trivial if it fails in some group. -/
def GroupIdentity.IsNontrivial (i : GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∃ G : GroupObject, ¬ SatisfiesIdentity G i

/-- A group quasivariety in which a non-trivial identity holds. -/
def IdentityBoundedQuasivariety :=
  {K : GroupQuasivariety //
    ∃ i : GroupIdentity, i.IsNontrivial ∧ ∀ G ∈ K.1, SatisfiesIdentity G i}

/-- The Mal'cev product of two classes of groups: `G` belongs to `K · L` when
it has a normal subgroup in `K` whose quotient belongs to `L`. -/
def malcevProduct (K L : GroupQuasivariety) : Set GroupObject :=
  {G | ∃ (N : Subgroup G) (hN : N.Normal),
    GroupObject.of N ∈ K.1 ∧ GroupObject.quotient G N hN ∈ L.1}

/--
Is the semigroup of all group quasivarieties in which a non-trivial identity
holds, under the Mal'cev product, a free semigroup? More precisely, does there
exist a type of generators and a bijection from its nonempty words to these
quasivarieties that carries concatenation to the Mal'cev product?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.55» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ X : Type 1, ∃ e : FreeSemigroup X ≃ IdentityBoundedQuasivariety,
      ∀ x y : FreeSemigroup X,
        (e (x * y)).1.1 = malcevProduct (e x).1 (e y).1 := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.55»
modeling_decisions: Groups are bundled in `GroupObject` with carriers in `Type`, fixing one universe so the collection of quasivarieties is a genuine Lean type.

A group quasivariety is represented extensionally as a set of bundled groups that is the model class of some set of finitary group quasi-identities. The chosen set of axioms is not part of the quasivariety object.

A non-trivial identity is defined semantically as an identity that fails in some group; an identity-bounded quasivariety has one such identity valid in every member, matching containment in a proper variety.
The Mal'cev product uses a normal subgroup in the left class and its quotient in the right class, in the order specified by the decomposition.

Freeness is expressed by an equivalence from Mathlib's `FreeSemigroup X` (nonempty words, not `FreeMonoid`) that preserves concatenation and the Mal'cev product. Product preservation is stated as equality of underlying group classes, which also encodes the required closure without introducing an unproved `Semigroup` instance.

  carrier : Set GrpCat.{0}

      ∀ x y : FreeSemigroup α,

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.55

by A. Yu. Olshanskii

It is easy to see that the set of all quasivarieties of groups, in each of which
quasivarieties a non-trivial identity holds, is a semigroup under multiplication of
quasivarieties. Is this semigroup free?

Here a *quasivariety* of groups is a class of groups consisting of all groups satisfying some
set of quasi-identities $w_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_n = 1 \Rightarrow w = 1$, where
$w_1, \dots, w_n, w$ are group words (elements of the free group on countably many variables)
and $n = 0$ is allowed, so that every identity is a quasi-identity. A non-trivial identity holds
in a class $\mathfrak{K}$ if there is a word $w \neq 1$ of the free group such that $w = 1$ in
every group of $\mathfrak{K}$. The multiplication is the Mal'cev product: a group $G$ lies in
$\mathfrak{K}\mathfrak{L}$ if and only if it has a normal subgroup $N \in \mathfrak{K}$ with
$G/N \in \mathfrak{L}$.

The trivial quasivariety $\mathfrak{E}$ belongs to this semigroup and is a two-sided identity
element for the Mal'cev product. As in the theorem of B. H. Neumann, H. Neumann, P. M. Neumann
and A. L. Šmel'kin that the varieties of groups other than the variety of all groups form a free
monoid under this multiplication, "free" is therefore understood as: the semigroup is
isomorphic to the free monoid on some set. Equivalently, its non-trivial members form a free
semigroup.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.55»

/-- A class of groups, modelled as a predicate on the groups whose carrier lives in `Type`. -/
abbrev GroupClass : Type 1 := (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop

/-- A quasi-identity in the language of groups: finitely many premises $w_i = 1$ and a
conclusion $w = 1$, where the $w_i$ and $w$ are group words, i.e. elements of the free group on
the countably many variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$. An identity is a quasi-identity without
premises. -/
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The words $w_1, \dots, w_n$ of the premises $w_1 = 1, \dots, w_n = 1$. -/
  premises : List (FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The word $w$ of the conclusion $w = 1$. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ

/-- A quasi-identity holds in a group `G` if for every assignment of the variables in `G`
(i.e. every homomorphism `FreeGroup ℕ →* G`) at which all the premises equal `1`, the
conclusion equals `1` as well. -/
def QuasiIdentity.HoldsIn (q : QuasiIdentity) (G : Type) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, (∀ w ∈ q.premises, φ w = 1) → φ q.conclusion = 1

/-- A class of groups is a quasivariety if it consists exactly of the groups in which all
quasi-identities from some set of quasi-identities hold. -/
def IsQuasivariety (K : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ Q : Set QuasiIdentity, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], K G ↔ ∀ q ∈ Q, q.HoldsIn G

/-- A non-trivial identity holds in the class of groups `K`: there is a word `w ≠ 1` of the
free group such that `w = 1` holds identically in every group of `K`. -/
def HasNontrivialIdentity (K : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ w : FreeGroup ℕ, w ≠ 1 ∧
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], K G → ∀ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, φ w = 1

/-- The Mal'cev product `K * L` of two classes of groups: the class of groups `G` having a
normal subgroup `N` with `N ∈ K` and `G / N ∈ L`. -/
def malcevMul (K L : GroupClass) : GroupClass :=
  fun G _ => ∃ (N : Subgroup G) (_ : N.Normal), K N ∧ L (G ⧸ N)

/-- The set of all quasivarieties of groups in each of which a non-trivial identity holds. -/
def quasivarietiesWithIdentity : Set GroupClass :=
  {K | IsQuasivariety K ∧ HasNontrivialIdentity K}

/-- The trivial class of groups, consisting of the trivial groups. -/
def trivialClass : GroupClass := fun G _ => ∀ g : G, g = 1

/-- The trivial class is defined by the identity $x_0 = 1$, so it is a quasivariety. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem isQuasivariety_trivialClass : IsQuasivariety trivialClass := by
  refine ⟨{⟨[], FreeGroup.of 0⟩}, fun G _ => ?_⟩
  simp only [trivialClass, Set.mem_singleton_iff, forall_eq, QuasiIdentity.HoldsIn,
    List.not_mem_nil, false_imp_iff, implies_true, true_imp_iff]
  refine ⟨fun h φ => h _, fun h g => ?_⟩
  simpa using h (FreeGroup.lift fun _ => g)

/-- The non-trivial identity $x_0 = 1$ holds in the trivial class. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem hasNontrivialIdentity_trivialClass : HasNontrivialIdentity trivialClass :=
  ⟨FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of_ne_one 0, fun _ _ h _ => h _⟩

/-- The trivial quasivariety belongs to the semigroup in question. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem trivialClass_mem_quasivarietiesWithIdentity :
    trivialClass ∈ quasivarietiesWithIdentity :=
  ⟨isQuasivariety_trivialClass, hasNontrivialIdentity_trivialClass⟩

/-- The class of all groups is a quasivariety (defined by the empty set of quasi-identities). -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem isQuasivariety_top : IsQuasivariety (fun _ _ => True) :=
  ⟨∅, fun _ _ => by simp⟩

/-- No non-trivial identity holds in the class of all groups, since it contains the free group,
so the class of all groups does not belong to the semigroup in question. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem top_notMem_quasivarietiesWithIdentity :
    (fun _ _ => True) ∉ quasivarietiesWithIdentity := by
  rintro ⟨-, w, hw, h⟩
  exact hw (h (FreeGroup ℕ) trivial (MonoidHom.id _))

/--
Is the semigroup of all quasivarieties of groups in each of which a non-trivial identity holds,
under the Mal'cev multiplication of quasivarieties, free?

Since the trivial quasivariety is a two-sided identity element of this semigroup, freeness is
stated as the existence of a multiplicative bijection from the free monoid on some set onto this
set of quasivarieties (equivalently, the non-trivial members form a free semigroup).
-/

    ∃ (X : Type) (f : FreeMonoid X → GroupClass), Function.Injective f ∧
      Set.range f = quasivarietiesWithIdentity ∧
      ∀ a b, f (a * b) = malcevMul (f a) (f b) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.55»

and a conclusion $w$, all words in the free group on the variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$, read as

quasivarieties a non-trivial identity holds, is a semigroup under multiplication of

quasivariety $\mathfrak{E}$ is excluded because it is the identity element of the semigroup

monoid.
-/

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.55

by A. Yu. Olshanskii

It is easy to see that the set of all quasivarieties of groups in each of which a non-trivial
identity holds is a semigroup under multiplication of quasivarieties. Is this semigroup free?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.55»

/-- A group whose carrier belongs to the fixed universe `u`. -/
structure GroupModel.{u} where
  carrier : Type u
  group : Group carrier

attribute [instance] GroupModel.group

/-- A finitary quasi-identity in the language of groups. Its premises and conclusion are
 equations between words in countably many variables. -/
structure GroupQuasiIdentity where
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ)
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ

/-- A group satisfies a quasi-identity if every assignment satisfying all its premises also
satisfies its conclusion. -/
def SatisfiesQuasiIdentity (G : GroupModel) (q : GroupQuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G.carrier,
    (∀ p ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift f p.1 = FreeGroup.lift f p.2) →
      FreeGroup.lift f q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift f q.conclusion.2

/-- A universe-bounded quasivariety of groups is a class axiomatized by a set of finitary
quasi-identities. -/
structure Quasivariety.{u} where
  groups : Set GroupModel.{u}
  axiomatizable : ∃ T : Set GroupQuasiIdentity,
    ∀ G, G ∈ groups ↔ ∀ q ∈ T, SatisfiesQuasiIdentity G q

instance : SetLike Quasivariety GroupModel where
  coe := Quasivariety.groups
  coe_injective' := fun K L h ↦ by cases K; cases L; simp_all

/-- A group satisfies the identity `lhs = rhs`. -/
def SatisfiesIdentity (G : GroupModel) (lhs rhs : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G.carrier, FreeGroup.lift f lhs = FreeGroup.lift f rhs

/-- Quasivarieties in which a non-trivial identity holds. Here non-trivial means that the two
words defining the identity are distinct in the free group. -/
def IdenticalQuasivariety.{u} :=
  {K : Quasivariety.{u} // ∃ lhs rhs : FreeGroup ℕ, lhs ≠ rhs ∧
    ∀ G ∈ K, SatisfiesIdentity G lhs rhs}

/-- `MalcevProduct K L M` says that `M` is the Mal'cev product of `K` and `L`: a group is in
`M` exactly when it has a normal subgroup in `K` whose quotient is in `L`. -/
def MalcevProduct.{u} (K L M : IdenticalQuasivariety.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ G : GroupModel.{u}, G ∈ M.1 ↔ ∃ N : Subgroup G.carrier, ∃ hN : N.Normal,
    (⟨N, inferInstance⟩ : GroupModel) ∈ K.1 ∧
    (⟨G.carrier ⧸ N, @QuotientGroup.Quotient.group G.carrier G.group N hN⟩ :
      GroupModel) ∈ L.1

/-- A relation `R` on a type presents a free semigroup if it is the graph of an associative
binary operation which, for some type of generators, is isomorphic to a free semigroup. -/
def IsFreeSemigroupUnder.{u} {S : Type u} (R : S → S → S → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ op : S → S → S, (∀ a b c, R a b c ↔ c = op a b) ∧ Std.Associative op ∧
    ∃ X : Type u, ∃ e : FreeSemigroup X ≃ S,
      ∀ a b, e (a * b) = op (e a) (e b)

/--
Is the semigroup of all group quasivarieties satisfying a non-trivial identity free under the
Mal'cev product? The collection is bounded to groups in one fixed universe. A quasivariety
belongs to it precisely when it is contained in the proper variety determined by some
non-trivial group identity.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.55» : answer(sorry) ↔
    IsFreeSemigroupUnder (@MalcevProduct.{0}) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.55»
modeling_decisions: Modeled the proper-class collection in the source using groups whose carriers lie in `Type 0`; the resulting collection of quasivarieties is a set-sized type in the next universe.

Defined a group quasivariety semantically as a universe-bounded class axiomatized by a set of finitary group quasi-identities. Group terms are represented by `FreeGroup ℕ`; countably many variables suffice because every term and every quasi-identity is finitary.

Read “a non-trivial identity holds” as existence of distinct free-group words whose induced equation is satisfied by every group in the quasivariety, equivalently containment in the proper variety defined by that identity.
Encoded the Mal'cev product by its specified membership condition: a group lies in `K·L` exactly when it has a normal subgroup in `K` with quotient in `L`.

Encoded “free” as free semigroup, not free monoid: the Mal'cev-product relation must be exactly the graph of an associative operation, and that semigroup must admit a multiplication-preserving bijection from `FreeSemigroup X` for some generating type `X`.

Included closure and associativity in the relational presentation of the semigroup. This reflects the asserted preamble while avoiding an unproved auxiliary closure theorem or a noncanonical chosen multiplication instance.
